title: Add up 13 numbers in how many reads?
hook: Running totals are quick to read but slow to change. One bit trick makes both quick.

doesNotKnow: that x & -x gives a hop that makes prefix sums and updates both take about log n cells

misconception: A running prefix-sum table is cheap to read, so changing one value only needs one cell touched.
objective: The learner can explain that a Fenwick cell i covers the last (i & -i) numbers up to i, so a prefix sum hops down by the lowest 1 bit (13 -> 12 -> 8: 3 reads for 13 numbers) and an update hops up by it (1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 cells), both about log2 n.

claims.text: Cell i of a Fenwick tree holds the sum of the last (i & -i) numbers up to position i, that is positions i - (i & -i) + 1 to i; i & -i is the lowest 1 bit of i.
claims.source: Fenwick (1994), 'A new data structure for cumulative frequency tables', Software: Practice and Experience 24(3) (citation from the brief: check before verifying). i & -i isolates the lowest set bit in two's complement (derivation: -i = ~i + 1).

claims.text: To add up the first 13 numbers you read cells 13, 12 and 8 (13 = 1101 loses its lowest 1 bit each hop); their ranges 13, 9-12 and 1-8 tile 1-13.
claims.source: Demo.tsx hopsDown(13); builder re-ran in Node (2026-10-14): [13..13], [9..12], [1..8]. Prefix 15 reads 15, 14, 12, 8 (4 cells); prefix 7 reads 7, 6, 4.

claims.text: On the stage numbers (3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 5 3 5 8 9 7 9 3) cells 13, 12 and 8 hold 9, 21 and 31, which add to 61, the sum of the first 13 numbers.
claims.source: Builder's Node run, 2026-10-14 (cells 1..16: 3 4 4 9 5 14 2 31 5 8 5 21 9 16 9 80; prefix 13 directly = 61). The numbers are fixed digits of pi, chosen for display only.

claims.text: Changing position 1 means updating the cells reached by hopping up by the lowest 1 bit: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, five cells; a plain running-total table would rewrite all 16.
claims.source: Demo.tsx hopsUp(1); builder re-ran in Node: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]. Running-total table: every prefix total 1..16 includes position 1 (derivation).

claims.text: Each hop down clears one 1 bit and each hop up moves the lowest 1 bit higher, so both take about log2 n steps.
claims.source: Down: i - lowbit(i) removes exactly one set bit, so at most popcount(i) <= floor(log2 n) + 1 hops. Up: i + lowbit(i) has a strictly higher lowest set bit, so at most floor(log2 n) + 1 hops within n. Fenwick (1994).

recall.question: In a Fenwick tree, the prefix sum up to position 22 (binary 10110) reads how many cells?
recall.why: One cell per 1 bit: 22 -> 20 -> 16 -> 0, reading cells 22, 20 and 16.
